clue.text: Somewhat astute sort, no mug, backing SPFL club

indicators.note: going backwards means the concealed letters are read from right to left
only some of the following words are used, so the letters lie inside a run of the clue

parts.note: the letters run across the end of astute, all of sort and no, and the start of mug

explanation.surface: A sharp-witted person, no fool, supporting a Scottish football club.
explanation.walkthrough: The SPFL is the Scottish Professional Football League; Montrose plays in its lower divisions.
explanation.definitionFit: Montrose FC is a Scottish football team competing in the SPFL, so it is an example of such a club.

clue.text: Design fashion line

parts.note: a mode is a style or fashion
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A designer working on a new range of clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A model is a particular design or version of a product, as in the latest car model.

clue.text: Hand cleaner new career after jumping bail

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: letters that are jumping leap about out of their order

parts.note: the word as written
to career is to rush headlong

explanation.surface: A criminal who skips bail and starts a new life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the hurry behind the reworked bail; jumping bail sounds like absconding but here it scrambles the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A nailbrush is a small brush for scrubbing fingernails, so it cleans hands.

clue.text: Bound to forget son learned fresh skills

indicators.note: what is forgotten is left out of the word

parts.note: bound and restrained both mean held fast
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A man was obliged to put his son out of his mind and took up new work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'certain to', but bound is the tied-up adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To be retrained is to be taught new abilities, especially for a different job.

clue.text: Number extremely sorry about result

indicators.note: being about something means surrounding it
the extremes of a word are its two ends

parts.note: the first and last letters of sorry
an event is an outcome or result

explanation.surface: Someone is deeply apologetic about how things turned out.
explanation.definitionFit: Seventy is a number, ten times seven.

clue.text: Opponents desire change

parts.note: South and West are opponents at the bridge table
an itch is a craving or longing

explanation.surface: Rivals both want things to be different.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge North-South play against East-West, so any compass pair such as S and W can be opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch is to swap or alter one thing for another, a verb synonym of change.

clue.text: Wind you and I have that's audible!

indicators.note: something audible is heard, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: the contraction of we have

explanation.surface: A rueful admission that the two of you have flatulence that can be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: To weave is to wind a twisting course, as through traffic or a crowd.

clue.text: Oscar exiting Cambridge exam falls over

indicators.note: a letter exiting a word leaves it

parts.note: the Tripos is the honours degree examination at Cambridge University
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A student named Oscar leaves his Cambridge finals and tumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar looks like a person but is the phonetic-alphabet letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Trips, as a verb, means stumbles and falls over.

clue.text: King in favour of essentially subsidising vehicle manufacturer

parts.note: Henry is the name of several English kings
being for something means supporting it

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, its central letter

parts.note: the sixth of eleven letters is the centre

explanation.surface: A monarch fundamentally backs public money for a carmaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Ford founded the Ford Motor Company and pioneered the mass production of cars.

clue.text: River rose perhaps

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a bloom, of which a rose is one example

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' for a river is a classic crossword trick: a river is something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a thing that flows, a flow-er in crossword logic, and a rose is an example of a bloom.

clue.text: Current import

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a flow of water or air carrying things along
second meaning: the general meaning or gist of something said

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like adjective and verb, but each is a noun here: current as in a stream, import as in significance.
explanation.definitionFit: A drift is a slow movement carried by a flow, and also the overall gist of an argument, as in 'get my drift'.

clue.text: Coarse person is very Eastern European, not British!

parts.note: V is the standard abbreviation for very

indicators.note: 'not' tells the solver to drop the letter standing for British from the word

parts.note: someone from Bulgaria in eastern Europe
B is an abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: An exclamation that some uncouth type is thoroughly continental rather than British.
explanation.definitionFit: A vulgarian is an unrefined, crude individual, so the noun matches a coarse person.

clue.text: Sign in public building Rosemary outwardly ignored

indicators.note: letters that are ignored are left out of the longer word

parts.note: a public library is a civic building

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the name

explanation.surface: A notice in a town hall that a woman called Rosemary was snubbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra, the scales, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: State of calf born recently?

parts.note: something newly born is new
a Jersey is a breed of dairy cattle, so the calf can be one

explanation.surface: Asking how a freshly delivered calf is doing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like condition but is a US state; the question mark flags that the calf is only one example of a Jersey animal.
explanation.definitionFit: New Jersey is one of the fifty states of the USA, named after the Channel Island that gave the cattle breed its name.

clue.text: Command pilot eats huge snack now and again

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside itself

parts.note: to pilot an aircraft is to fly it

indicators.note: something done now and again happens only at intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of the two words run together

explanation.surface: An order that an airman has been scoffing an enormous bite intermittently.
explanation.definitionFit: Command of a language means mastery of it, which is fluency: speaking or writing it easily.

clue.text: Bird food, ground at first

parts.note: a field is a sports ground
fare is food provided

explanation.surface: Bird food is ground up before serving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' places the ground before the food; 'ground' looks like a milled past participle, but it is a playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: The fieldfare is a large thrush that winters in Britain.

clue.text: Gentleman rejected excessive outlay originally making dish

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the title is written backwards

parts.note: sir is the form of address for a gentleman
OTT is short for over the top

indicators.note: originally points to the origin of the word, its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of outlay

explanation.surface: A man turned down a spending plan that was extravagant from the start, which led to a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Rod, glowing at times, supports boss in game

parts.note: a stud or boss is a raised knob on a surface
a fire poker is a metal rod that glows when left in the coals

explanation.surface: A rod that sometimes glows is propping up a manager in some contest.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the supporter sits below, so the rod goes after the boss; boss looks like a manager but is a stud.
explanation.definitionFit: Stud poker is a form of the card game in which some cards are dealt face up.

clue.text: Film director with star discovered travelling on train

indicators.note: dis-covered means stripped of its covering, the outside letters

parts.note: the word with its first and last letters taken off

indicators.note: letters that are travelling move around from their places

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A director spotted a celebrity on a rail journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Quentin Tarantino is the American film-maker behind Pulp Fiction and Kill Bill.

clue.text: Animal emerging from hacienda, endlessly barking

indicators.note: a word without its end has lost its final letter
barking is slang for mad, so the letters go haywire

parts.note: the Spanish ranch with its last letter removed

explanation.surface: A creature comes out of a ranch house, yapping all the while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' fits the animal picture as noise, but it is slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna is a spiny egg-laying mammal of Australia and New Guinea.

clue.text: Person who draws handcart is transporting boxes

indicators.note: what boxes something holds it inside, so the letters are enclosed in the words

parts.note: spans the end of handcart, all of is and the start of transporting

explanation.surface: A worker pulling a barrow carries crates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person who draws' suggests someone hauling a cart, which the surface reinforces; it means someone who draws pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist makes drawings and pictures, so is a person who draws.

clue.text: Visibly embarrassed after rock band gets woozy

parts.note: Blur is a British rock band of the Britpop era
blushing shows embarrassment as a red face

explanation.surface: A musician blushes after the gig and then feels dizzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the blushing colour behind the band's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Woozy describes vision or thinking that has become unclear, and blurred means indistinct in the same way.

clue.text: Secure set of rules for one given a scan

parts.note: to bar a door is to secure it
a code is a body of rules

explanation.surface: Lock in a rulebook for a patient going for a medical scan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given a scan' points to hospitals, but the scan is at a supermarket checkout.
explanation.definitionFit: A barcode is the striped label read by a scanner at a till, so it is something scanned.

clue.text: Last month, one speaking who sometimes appears plastered?

definitions.note: read with 'one' from the wordplay: one who sometimes appears plastered

parts.note: DEC is the calendar abbreviation for December
an orator is a public speaker

explanation.surface: Someone giving a speech in December is apparently often drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastered' suggests drunkenness; here it means covered in plaster, as a painter and decorator often is.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorator plasters, paints and papers rooms, so may be literally plastered at work.

clue.text: Distressed trade unionists?

parts.note: surface reading: union members who are upset
setter's reading: the abbreviation for trade unionists runs upward, read backwards in this down entry, inside the answer

explanation.surface: Union members are upset about something.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags whimsy: the TU of trade unions appears turned upward inside the answer, as though cut up.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cut up is an informal idiom for being very upset or distressed.

clue.text: Heads to roll investigating people operating northern racecourse

indicators.note: the head of each word is its opening letter

parts.note: the initial letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: Dismissals are coming for officials in a probe into staff working up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads to roll' reads as sackings, but heads are first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripon in North Yorkshire has a well-known horse-racing course.

clue.text: Long to get back to 1960s clothing

parts.note: to pant for something is to long for it

indicators.note: the back of an item is its final character

parts.note: the final character of the decade as written

explanation.surface: Wanting to return to the fashions of the swinging sixties.
explanation.definitionFit: Pants are trousers or underpants, a garment and so clothing.

clue.text: Criminal takes something from the butcher's

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A thief pinches goods from a meat shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Steak is a cut of beef sold by a butcher.

clue.text: Hors d'oeuvre Pat's into cooking, hosting American

indicators.note: a host has a guest inside the home
ingredients being cooked are mixed and transformed

parts.note: the letters as written, apostrophe dropped
A is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Pat enjoys making starters and is entertaining a visitor from the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian course of cold meats and appetisers served before the main meal, an hors d'oeuvre.

clue.text: Dirk, say, flipping popular amongst English folk on vacation

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it the other way round

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: one item placed amongst others sits in their midst
a vacated place is emptied, leaving only the outer letters of the word

parts.note: only the first and last letters remain
something in is fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A man named Dirk is extremely well liked among English people on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Dirk looks like a man's name, but a dirk is a Scottish dagger, an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirk is a long dagger, a kind of bladed weapon, hence an example signalled by 'say'.

clue.text: Go through report of West Country banker put on paper

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words are judged by sound

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, and a river is a banker because it has banks
to pen is to write down

explanation.surface: Going over a news story about a West Country bank employee written up in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: Banker is crossword shorthand for a river; the West Country is south-west England, where the Exe flows.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through money is to spend or use it up, which is what expend means.

clue.text: Annual bore, okay when broadcast

indicators.note: seed that is broadcast is scattered in all directions, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: the letters of the two words as written

explanation.surface: A yearly programme that is tedious but acceptable on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Annual' looks like an adjective, but as a noun it is a book published once a year.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual is a book issued once a year, just as a yearbook is.
